stories.title: A pancreatic cancer vaccine drew immune responses in nearly every patient
stories.summary: In a randomised phase 2 trial led by a Mayo Clinic researcher, nearly every patient who got the vaccine developed an immune response against mutated KRAS, found in about 90 percent of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas. ScienceAlert notes this does not prove it stops the cancer returning.

stories.title: Japan treats its first patient with a stem cell therapy for Parkinson's
stories.summary: A patient has undergone a stem cell therapy for Parkinson's disease, the Japanese drugmaker behind it said on Friday, a world first following the treatment's conditional approval in Japan, Medical Xpress reports. The treatment's long term results are yet to be reported.

stories.title: FDA drops black box warnings on three more menopause patches without advisers
stories.summary: Three more menopause patches will no longer carry black box warnings about cardiovascular disease, breast cancer and dementia, the FDA said on Friday. It did not convene an advisory committee and offered few details on the science, the Guardian reports. Six treatments lost warnings earlier.

stories.title: High dose omega 3 may lengthen survival in some advanced colon cancer
stories.summary: A trial found some patients with advanced colon cancer who took high daily doses of the omega 3 fat EPA had higher five year overall survival, HealthDay reports. The cancer was not stopped completely, and the finding applies only to some patients.

stories.title: A tumour atlas looks at why colorectal cancer hits young patients harder
stories.summary: Dana-Farber's Kimmie Ng published a Nature Medicine study mapping colorectal tumours to find biological differences in early onset cases, STAT reports. Patients under 35 may fare worse than people in their 40s or 60s despite more aggressive treatment and better baseline health.

stories.title: Fish oil did not protect thinking in people at risk of Alzheimer's
stories.summary: A two year trial of high dose omega 3 in older adults at raised risk of Alzheimer's found no improvement in memory, thinking or brain structure, Healthline reports. Omega 3 levels rose in the blood and brain fluid. The test scores did not follow.

stories.title: Albumin does not prevent kidney injury in intensive care, review finds
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of nine randomised trials with 11,778 patients, published in Critical Care, found human serum albumin, widely used for fluid resuscitation in intensive care, did not significantly reduce acute kidney injury in critically ill patients.

stories.title: Patients treated by female doctors in hospital may do better
stories.summary: An ICES study led by a University of Toronto researcher found patients cared for by female physicians in hospital were less likely to die or be readmitted than those treated by male physicians, Medical Xpress reports. The researchers describe an association.

stories.title: Review finds no evidence testosterone helps menopause brain fog
stories.summary: A UCL study says there is not enough evidence to determine whether testosterone helps thinking and memory in midlife women, even though it is often prescribed in the UK for that reason, Medical Xpress reports.

stories.title: Prednisolone gave long Covid patients a modest, short lived lift
stories.summary: A treatment trial of the steroid prednisolone for post Covid syndrome showed a modest and short lived improvement, Medical Xpress reports. Reliable data on which treatments work for persistent fatigue, breathlessness and concentration problems remain scarce.

stories.title: Keralam study finds distinct gut bacteria in Parkinson's patients
stories.summary: Researchers from CUSAT and SCTIMST in Thiruvananthapuram found significant differences between the gut bacteria of Parkinson's patients and healthy people, in a study published in npj Parkinson's Disease, The Hindu reports. Scientists have long suspected the gut and brain talk constantly.

stories.title: Air pollution aged bone marrow stem cells faster in diabetic mice
stories.summary: A mouse study found fine particulate matter can accelerate ageing in bone marrow stem cells and weaken their ability to regenerate, with stronger effects in mice with type 2 diabetes, the Indian Express reports. The findings so far come from mice.

stories.title: Blocking one molecular interaction reduced heart scarring in mice
stories.summary: Researchers at Baylor College of Medicine and the University of Oxford found blocking a specific molecular interaction reduced atrial fibrosis and abnormal rhythms in mouse models and in cells from patients with atrial fibrillation, Medical Xpress reports. It is early stage work.

stories.title: Regulators halted Sun Pharma's eye drug production at its Assam plant
stories.summary: The CDSCO and Assam's drugs controller ordered Sun Pharmaceutical to stop making, selling and distributing ophthalmic products from its Assam facility on 20 August, after finding failures in its quality management system, documents reviewed by Reuters show, The Hindu reports.

stories.title: India recorded over two lakh new breast cancer cases in 2024
stories.summary: India reported more than two lakh new breast cancer cases in 2024, with an estimated one in 29 women at risk, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said while launching commemorative breast cancer awareness stamps. She stressed early detection, the New Indian Express reports.

stories.title: Most breast complaints at a Mumbai cancer institute were cancer
stories.summary: A review of 578 patients at the Head and Neck Cancer Institute of India, Mumbai, found 82.5 percent had cancerous conditions, confirmed by tissue examination, The Hindu reports. The authors say it reflects patients at one institute and cannot be generalised.

stories.title: Imported drugs must now carry at least a year of shelf life
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has replaced the 60 per cent residual shelf life rule with a fixed 12 month minimum for most imported drugs, aiming to ease imports and reduce wastage, Business Standard reports.

stories.title: Karnataka pauses its hospital medicine price disclosure rule
stories.summary: The state told the Karnataka High Court it will not insist for now on a circular requiring hospital pharmacies to show purchase price and MRP of medicines, devices and consumables on bills, The Hindu reports. Patients will continue to see the one number.

stories.title: Stroke makes up 40% of NIMHANS neurology casualty cases
stories.summary: Nearly 40 per cent of patients at the NIMHANS neurology casualty have stroke, about 705 cases a month, The Hindu reports. A hub and spoke link with the Karnataka institute in Hubballi, which treats about 120 cases a month, extends stroke care north.

stories.title: Mothers' feeding habits shape children's fussiness about new foods
stories.summary: An ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition study in the Journal of Nutritional Science found a mother's knowledge, attitude and feeding practices significantly influence a child's willingness to try new foods, and calls for stronger nutrition counselling for caregivers, The Hindu reports.

stories.title: Why the stigma around TB refuses to go away
stories.summary: A 26 year old diagnosed with tuberculosis was told by a family friend to tell nobody at work except HR and her manager, the Indian Express reports, in a piece on how old beliefs about TB still shape how patients are treated.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh releases Rs 9.86 crore for 16 de-addiction centres
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh has released Rs 9.86 crore through its Prohibition and Excise Department to modernise 16 drug de-addiction centres in government hospitals, with a focus on treatment, counselling and rehabilitation, The Hindu reports.

stories.title: Keralam orders 2,159 bottles of an oral SMA drug
stories.summary: Keralam has issued orders to buy 2,159 bottles of Risdiplam, the first at home oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, to keep supplies steady, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan told the Assembly, The Hindu reports. The programme runs through the state's KARE rare disease initiative.

stories.title: Private equity in Indian health went mostly to the west and south
stories.summary: A Brown University and Johns Hopkins study of 70 private equity backed acquisitions from 2007 to May 2025 found over 73 per cent of investment went to 45 hospital groups, mostly in urban southern and western states, ET HealthWorld reports. Rural regions got little.

stories.title: The Centre reviews vacations for government medical college doctors
stories.summary: A Union health ministry expert committee is examining vacation and academic leave for Central Health Service teaching doctors and has sought records from three Delhi institutions, ET HealthWorld reports. The question is what happens to patients and classes during summer and winter breaks.

stories.title: Doctors at a summit say dengue needs more than a vaccine
stories.summary: At the India Today HealthWealth Summit, experts said dengue prevention needs public awareness, timely diagnosis and year round mosquito control alongside vaccination. Dr Kataria said young people with strong immunity are most vulnerable to severe dengue.

stories.title: Africa CDC says the Ebola response is falling behind
stories.summary: With confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases above 10,000 and nearly 5,000 deaths, Africa CDC Director General Dr Jean Kaseya told more than 40 African health ministers on 28 October that the response is falling behind, The National reports.

stories.title: Minnesota sees its most measles cases in 36 years
stories.summary: Minnesota has reported 80 measles cases in 2026, its highest in 36 years, with 57 in Todd County since mid September, MPR News reports. Health officials attribute the outbreak to a vaccination rate that was below average and has dropped further.

stories.title: More US families choose an earlier second measles shot
stories.summary: With twice as many confirmed US measles cases as last year, more parents are opting for the second MMR dose early, as soon as four weeks after the first, the Guardian reports. Germany, the UK and France already recommend a similar schedule.

stories.title: MPs say England's obesity plan is doomed without a rethink
stories.summary: The health and social care select committee says the government's moonshot ambition to reverse rising obesity within a decade is doomed to fail without a new plan led directly by the prime minister, the Guardian reports. Moonshots usually come with a rocket.

stories.title: FDA investigates a Salmonella outbreak with no known food source
stories.summary: The FDA has opened an investigation into a Salmonella Javiana outbreak with 59 illnesses, according to its 28 October update, Medical Daily reports. It has not identified the food or said where patients live or their ages.

stories.title: Saskatchewan sees a rise in meningococcal disease
stories.summary: Saskatchewan has recorded 15 cases of invasive meningococcal disease so far in 2026 after 16 in 2025, against fewer than five in a typical year, chief medical health officer Saqib Shahab said. The cases involve the W135 strain, uncommon in western Canada.

stories.title: One in four Americans have faked symptoms to get antibiotics
stories.summary: A survey of nearly 1,000 Americans found more than a quarter had exaggerated or made up symptoms to try to get antibiotics for themselves or their children, Medical Xpress reports. The doctors, presumably, were told it was very bad.

stories.title: Genomes from Ethiopia's first Marburg outbreak show human transmission
stories.summary: A Nature Microbiology analysis of seven near complete Marburg virus genomes from early cases of Ethiopia's first outbreak, reported in November 2025 with a 64 percent fatality rate, places it in the MARV.A.1 clade and points to human transmission after spillover.

stories.title: HHS clears six experimental peptides despite FDA scientists' concerns
stories.summary: HHS issued a policy letting licensed pharmacies and physicians temporarily compound six experimental peptides, including BPC-157 and TB-500, without fear of federal enforcement, STAT reports. FDA career scientists objected that there is scant evidence they are safe or effective.

stories.title: Israel's health ministry warns against illegal weight loss peptides
stories.summary: Israel's Health Ministry warned against illegal peptides marketed for weight loss and bodybuilding, including BPC-157, GHK-Cu, CJC-1295, TB-500 and retatrutide, which is still in clinical trials and not approved there, Ynetnews reports. The substances are marketed for weight loss and bodybuilding.

stories.title: Namibia steps up Ebola checks at its borders
stories.summary: Namibia's health ministry has heightened disease surveillance and strengthened preparedness at points of entry after Ebola outbreaks in several African countries, the Namibia Economist reports. Officials confirmed no suspected or confirmed cases have been detected in the country.

stories.title: Uganda's health officials warn the country to expect more epidemics
stories.summary: Officials and scientists at Kampala's Joint Annual Scientific Health conference warned Uganda to prepare for more emerging epidemics driven by shifting environmental patterns and climate change, alongside a rising burden of non communicable diseases as the population ages, the Daily Monitor reports.

stories.title: Flu season starts unusually early in Canada's Northwest Territories
stories.summary: Flu season began in early October in the Northwest Territories and across Canada, and people were already sick as vaccine clinics opened, Cabin Radio reports. Chief public health officer Dr Kami Kandola said it usually starts in November or December.

stories.title: People with HIV now lose more years of life to smoking than to HIV
stories.summary: About 1.2 million Americans live with HIV, and while adult smoking in the US has fallen below 10 per cent, people with HIV smoke at up to four times that rate, Medical Xpress reports. Many of them want to quit.

stories.title: IIT Gandhinagar and AIIMS build a Hindi tool to screen for aphasia
stories.summary: Researchers from IIT Gandhinagar and AIIMS New Delhi have developed CHASP, a computerised Hindi language platform to help clinicians spot aphasia, the speech and language disorder that often follows stroke, in resource constrained settings where diagnosis is delayed, Elets eHealth reports.

stories.title: Data brokers track patients to the clinic and sell the inference
stories.summary: KFF Health News reports data brokers use phone location data to infer health conditions and sell them to firms touting unproven treatments. Chris McQueen, who finished leukaemia treatment, still gets ads for juice cleanses that cure cancer during routine oncologist visits.

stories.title: Nearly two in three US teens and tweens use AI chatbots
stories.summary: Two new surveys show nearly two thirds of American tweens and teens use AI chatbots, mostly for schoolwork but also for companionship and emotional support, NPR reports. Certain uses were linked with worse mental health symptoms.

stories.title: FDA and CMS try to head off a state versus federal AI clash
stories.summary: Federal health officials are working behind the scenes as more states look to test AI in clinical settings, STAT reports. States regulate the practice of medicine, the FDA regulates devices, and AI that writes prescriptions now falls under both.

stories.title: Dexcom raises its 2026 outlook as revenue grows 11%
stories.summary: Glucose monitor maker Dexcom reported third quarter revenue of $1.344 billion, up 11 per cent from $1.209 billion, raised its full year 2026 outlook and authorised up to $1 billion in share buybacks, Securities.io reports.

stories.title: Digital health helps rural African clinics only where systems are ready
stories.summary: A review of 35 studies from 18 countries, in BMC Digital Health, found digital health tools in rural sub Saharan Africa succeed far less because of the technology than because of the readiness of the health systems receiving them.

stories.title: Kenya gives hospitals until 30 November to switch health systems
stories.summary: Kenya's Social Health Authority and Digital Health Agency extended by a month the deadline for facilities to migrate to approved digital health management information systems, saying the delay avoids disruption to patient services, The Star reports.

stories.title: WHO Europe reports progress on its digital health action plan
stories.summary: WHO Europe's biennial progress report on its 2023 to 2030 regional digital health action plan reviews work across 18 focus areas in all 53 member states from June 2024 to March 2026, including guidance on using data for better health decisions.

stories.title: Evaxion wins an international Prix Galien for its AI immunology platform
stories.summary: Danish company Evaxion, which develops immunotherapies using its AI-Immunology platform, received the 2026 International Prix Galien Award for best digital health solution, according to its own announcement. The company calls it yet another important external recognition.

stories.title: The Lancet says the online manosphere is a public health issue
stories.summary: A report in The Lancet says the social media manosphere, online communities built around masculinity, misogyny and male victimhood, should be treated as a public health issue much like the tobacco industry, the New Indian Express reports.

stories.title: Job support kept people with schizophrenia employed far longer
stories.summary: In a three year randomised study at one hospital in southern China, people with schizophrenia who received case management plus supported employment worked a median of 25 months, much longer than those who searched for jobs alone, Bioengineer reports.

stories.title: Mental health problems after cancer linked to higher cancer deaths
stories.summary: A Stanford Medicine study found mental health disorders identified two to five years after a cancer diagnosis were associated with a 119 per cent higher rate of death from cancer, pointing to an overlooked period of vulnerability, Medical Xpress reports.

stories.title: Costs are widening the gap in timely mental health care in Australia
stories.summary: Research reported by newsGP finds high out of pocket costs and slow moving Medicare subsidies are stopping many lower income Australians from following through with mental health treatment, creating a growing income divide in access.

stories.title: Floods linked to more mental health problems in four African countries
stories.summary: A study of 5,336 people in Burkina Faso, Kenya, Mozambique and South Africa estimated that the sample would have had 25 per cent fewer mental health problems without floods, comparing people who experienced floods with those who did not, TimesLIVE reports.

stories.title: Adventurous outdoor play may help children's health, review finds
stories.summary: A review of 74 studies led by the University of Exeter and the University of British Columbia, published on 26 October, suggests letting children climb, balance and explore outdoors on their own may support their physical and mental health, Yahoo Health reports.

stories.title: Teens spot mental health problems but rarely plan to get help
stories.summary: A mixed methods study in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health found adolescents who accurately identify mental health problems in others often say they would not turn to professional services themselves. Internalising disorders were recognised most accurately.

stories.title: Review pools mental health data on Gulf university students
stories.summary: A BMC Psychiatry review of 46 studies with more than 24,600 university students in Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE examined depression, anxiety and stress symptoms reported between 2010 and 2025, Sharjah24 reports.

stories.title: Telling life stories can support recovery from personality disorders
stories.summary: UT PhD research by a clinical psychologist shows personal life stories, covering who you are, what shaped you and how you see your future, can support treatment and personal recovery for people with personality disorders, Medical Xpress reports.

research.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months
research.summary: A promising new study suggests that more than half of younger adults with type 2 diabetes could achieve remission in just six months through a combination of a low-calorie diet and structured exercise. Researchers found that 54% of participants under age 45 who followed an intensive diet and.

research.title: Why some “lower-risk” childhood cancers turn deadly
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered hidden aggressive cancer cells in children whose tumors were previously considered lower risk, revealing why some cases of rhabdomyosarcoma become unexpectedly deadly. The discovery could help doctors identify dangerous tumors earlier and develop personalized treatments that improve survival while reducing unnecessary chemotherapy.
